item.title: GovBrief Today #658
item.description: The Interior Department auctioned the mining rights to 31 million acres of Pacific seafloor today for about 19 cents an acre. Before the sale, the law required the government to check whether it would harm endangered species. Its answer was a four-page letter that addressed the first steps but left out the effects of mining. On Monday a federal judge ruled that the letter broke the Endangered Species Act. She called the review “cramped, expedited, informal” but did not order the auction halted. Interior’s mining office said it answered her by starting a new review, then held the sale anyway. Wetstone U.S. Ventures, a startup, was the sole bidder and won the mining rights to both tracts near American Samoa at the minimum bid of $3 million each. The leases run 20 years and let it mine if later reviews allow it. The government is considering auctions off the Northern Mariana Islands, Virginia, and Alaska. On February 1, 2025, I typed a list of nine things I never imagined a government doing in one day and sent it to my family. I’ve sent one every night since: 10,019 stories over 658 straight nights, free and without ads. Add your email address at govbrief.today and I’ll send it to you too. NEW: Zoom In is now live! item.description: Rockstar made people wait 13 years between Grand Theft Auto games, and $7.25 an hour still outlasted them. I'm sorry, but that's embarrassing. The federal minimum has been $7.25 since July 24, 2009. GTA V came out more than four years after that raise. GTA 6 just dropped. Two full games, and the floor for American workers hasn't moved one cent. Seventeen years, y'all. And here's the money part that gets me. The standard edition is $79.99. At $7.25 an hour, that's about 11 hours of work before taxes for one game. A full 40-hour week at that rate pays $290 before taxes, so the game alone eats more than a quarter of the check. Now, before somebody says most states already set their minimum higher, I agree. A lot of them do, and plenty of employers pay above it too. But here's where I have a problem. The federal number is still the floor wherever a state never set a higher one. And a floor that sits still for 17 years while rent and groceries keep climbing isn't protecting anybody. Gamers waited 13 years for this one. Workers stuck at $7.25 have waited 17, and nobody's even given them a release date....

item.title: Russell Brand Speedruns the Prison Difficulty Settings (Any% Glitchless)
item.description:
Russell Brand has apparently discovered that prison is not, in fact, another episode of his fucking podcast. According to reports, the convicted sex offender had his wife read a statement on YouTube protesting his innocence.
Fair enough. Prisoners can maintain their innocence. But then the absolute fucking genius announced which prison he was being held in. The prison where he'd reportedly been placed partly for his own protection. And now officials are considering transferring him somewhere considerably more restrictive. You couldn't script this shit. Imagine being handed a relatively safer prison placement and thinking, You know what this situation needs? A public announcement to 6.6 million subscribers. The man who built a career telling everyone to question authority has apparently forgotten that prison authorities can question him right back. His calls could now face closer monitoring, his communications are under scrutiny, and the possibility of a transfer is being discussed. All because he apparently couldn't go five fucking minutes without broadcasting. The most remarkable thing about Russell Brand isn't his ability to talk. It's his apparent inability to recognize when shutting the fuck up might be in his own best interests. And somewhere, his solicitor is probably staring silently at a wall. #RussellBrand #UKNews #Accountability #Prison #PoliticalSatire #BritishComedy #Imgur https://www.thetimes.com/uk/crime/article/russell-brand-prison-transfer-youtube-video-7z6jrf0s6 https://smry.ai/s/nYjPoWpO?ref=01NCHFKI
